test_1_lens_spec.test: if the scale were the gate inversion, the 789 px lens would be about 12.1 mm; is that plausible for the product
searched: docs/FM3 Edge Algorithm URS Final Draft .pdf (received)
what_exists: the URS names the product only as a contact lens and describes it as HEMA based (section 5.2.1, excess lens material); it gives no diameter, no brand and no product name
the Ontology gives no lens dimension, only annotation-box size statistics in pixels
the received set carries no lens diameter, no soft or rigid label and no product identifier
what_does_not_exist: no received document names the lens product, its size, its material beyond HEMA or its type (soft, rigid, daily, scleral)
no document names a 14.2 mm diameter either; the 14.2 mm used in our work is our own assumed figure
test_1_lens_spec.result: not available from the received documents. No received document states a lens diameter, so the physical plausibility of 12.1 mm against 14.2 mm cannot be settled from our documents. The general product class does not favour 12.1 mm: a soft hydrogel contact lens is normally about 13.8 to 14.5 mm across, and a 12.1 mm lens would sit below the usual range, so 14.2 mm is the more plausible diameter for a soft lens while neither is documented here.

test_2_multiple_lenses.class: Multiple Lenses (P1_ML), folder-derived tag on 1,439 pictures

finding.result: The class does not present two resolvable full lens circles, so it does not give the within-frame lens-diameter repeatability the test sought.
numbers: sample: 148 Multiple Lenses frames and 149 single-lens Clear control frames, all measured ok
rim circle diameter: Multiple Lenses 791.1 px (IQR 772.1 to 816.4) against control 808.6 px (IQR 789.1 to 820.2)

a two-circle split of the rim edge points improves the residual on 0.0 percent of Multiple Lenses frames and 0.0 percent of control frames (median ratio rms1/rms2 0.81 against 0.74, always below 1, so the split always fits worse)
at least one dark ring in the cavity interior (normalised radius below 0.80) appears on 38.5 percent of Multiple Lenses frames against 11.4 percent of control frames, 73 rings against 17
the interior ring sits at median normalised radius 0.58 on Multiple Lenses against 0.74 on control, so the extra boundary is a smaller partial circle, not a second full lens at the rim
within-frame rim residual (the repeatability of one rim measurement) is 19.6 px on Multiple Lenses against 17.6 px on control
finding.repeatability: not available from within-frame lens pairs, because no frame yields two resolved lens circles. The class does contain a second dark boundary on 57 of 148 frames, at median 0.58 of the cavity radius, consistent with the URS description of one lens plus an additional partial lens, but a partial lens at 0.58 R_cav is not a second full lens and yields no diameter pair.
finding.stability_reference: not answered by this class either: with no two resolved rims there is no second measure of the same part to compare against the cavity.

test_3_second_ruler.reason: the two frames whose second component reaches half the largest are Package Misalignment frames where the field of view is partly blocked, not a second cavity; no frame has the largest bright component touching the frame border, so no package or tray edge is imaged in frame; the many small second components sit at a near-fixed position above the cavity and are package features of unknown real length, so they give no scale. Every frame is one cavity, matching the CavityNN naming of the production drop.

test_4_box_margin.definition: at a scale S the gate switches on a longest box side of 19.41 to 19.61 px; a 300 micron debris at scale S spans 300/S px; the gap is the required annotation margin

deciding_number.result: the margin test does not separate the readings, and it makes the 18 micron scale the more comfortable one rather than the less

deciding_numbers.at_18_0_um_per_px: the box would be 2.743 to 2.943 px larger than a 300 micron debris, that is 14.06 to 15.09 percent of the box, about 1.42 px on each side
deciding_numbers.at_15_337_um_per_px: the box would be -0.151 to 0.049 px larger than a 300 micron debris, that is -0.77 to 0.25 percent of the box, essentially zero

deciding_number.reading: a hand-drawn box around a speck about 17 px across overshooting by about 2.8 px is a normal, small margin, so a 14 to 15 percent overshoot is plausible and does not falsify the lens-implied scale; a zero margin is also plausible, so the margin test is consistent with both readings and decides neither
